fields.title: Two Sum
fields.description: Given an array of integers nums and an integer target, return the indices of the two numbers such that they add up to target. Assume exactly one solution exists and you may not use the same element twice.

fields.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
fields.description: Given an array prices where prices[i] is the stock price on day i, find the maximum profit achievable by buying on one day and selling on a later day. Return 0 if no profit is possible.

fields.title: Maximum Subarray
fields.description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray (containing at least one number) which has the largest sum, and return that sum.

fields.title: Product of Array Except Self
fields.description: Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] equals the product of all elements of nums except nums[i], without using division and in O(n) time.

examples.explanation: Each entry is product of all others.

fields.title: Merge Intervals
fields.description: Given an array of intervals where intervals[i] = [start, end], merge all overlapping intervals and return an array of the non-overlapping intervals that cover all the input intervals.

fields.title: Valid Anagram
fields.description: Given two strings s and t, return true if t is an anagram of s, and false otherwise.
constraints: s and t consist of lowercase English letters.

fields.title: Valid Palindrome
fields.description: Given a string s, return true if it is a palindrome after converting all uppercase letters to lowercase and removing all non-alphanumeric characters.
constraints: s consists of printable ASCII characters.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"
examples.explanation: Ignoring case/punctuation it reads the same both ways.

fields.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
fields.description: Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
constraints: s consists of English letters, digits, symbols and spaces.

fields.title: Group Anagrams
fields.description: Given an array of strings strs, group the anagrams together. You can return the answer in any order.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: Words sharing sorted-letter keys are grouped.
Single empty string is its own group.

fields.title: Longest Common Prefix
fields.description: Write a function to find the longest common prefix string amongst an array of strings. If there is no common prefix, return an empty string.
constraints: strs[i] consists of lowercase English letters.

fields.title: Reverse Linked List
fields.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, reverse the list and return the new head.

fields.title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
fields.description: You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists. Merge them into one sorted list by splicing together the nodes and return its head.
constraints: Both lists are sorted in ascending order.

fields.title: Detect Cycle in Linked List
fields.description: Given the head of a linked list, determine if the linked list has a cycle in it, using O(1) extra memory.

examples.explanation: There is a cycle back to index 1.

fields.title: Remove Nth Node From End of List
fields.description: Given the head of a linked list, remove the nth node from the end of the list and return its head.

examples.explanation: The 2nd node from end (4) is removed.

fields.title: Middle of the Linked List
fields.description: Given the head of a singly linked list, return the middle node. If there are two middle nodes, return the second one.

examples.explanation: Second middle node returned for even length.

fields.title: Valid Parentheses
fields.description: Given a string s containing just the characters '(', ')', '{', '}', '[' and ']', determine if the input string is valid, meaning every bracket is closed in the correct order.
constraints: s consists only of bracket characters.

fields.title: Min Stack
fields.description: Design a stack that supports push, pop, top, and retrieving the minimum element in constant time.

examples.input: push(-2), push(0), push(-3), getMin(), pop(), top(), getMin()
examples.explanation: getMin returns the current minimum after each operation.

fields.title: Implement Queue using Stacks
fields.description: Implement a first-in-first-out (FIFO) queue using only two stacks, supporting push, pop, peek and empty operations.
constraints: At most 100 calls made to push, pop, peek, and empty.

examples.explanation: Queue behaves FIFO despite using stacks internally.
Queue is empty after popping the only element.

fields.title: Daily Temperatures
fields.description: Given an array of daily temperatures, return an array answer such that answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after day i to get a warmer temperature. If no future day exists, answer[i] = 0.

examples.explanation: Monotonic stack tracks days waiting for warmth.
Each day is warmer than the last.

fields.title: Next Greater Element
fields.description: Given two arrays nums1 and nums2 where nums1 is a subset of nums2, for each element in nums1 find the next greater element to its right in nums2. Return -1 if none exists.
constraints: All integers in nums1 and nums2 are unique.

examples.explanation: No greater element after 4; 3 follows 1; none after 2.

fields.title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
fields.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return its maximum depth, i.e. the number of nodes along the longest path from root to a leaf.

fields.title: Invert Binary Tree
fields.description: Given the root of a binary tree, invert the tree (swap every left and right child) and return its root.

examples.explanation: Left and right subtrees swapped at every node.
Empty tree inverted is still empty.

fields.title: Validate Binary Search Tree
fields.description: Given the root of a binary tree, determine if it is a valid binary search tree (BST), where every node's left subtree values are less and right subtree values are greater.

examples.explanation: Node 4's left child 3 is less than root 5 but violates local BST rule.

fields.title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
fields.description: Given the root of a binary tree, return the level order traversal of its nodes' values (i.e., from left to right, level by level).

fields.title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a BST
fields.description: Given a binary search tree and two nodes p and q, find their lowest common ancestor (LCA) in the BST.
constraints: p and q exist in the tree.

examples.explanation: 6 is the split point between the two subtrees.
4 is a descendant of 2, so 2 is the LCA.

fields.title: Number of Islands
fields.description: Given an m x n 2D binary grid representing '1' (land) and '0' (water), return the number of islands, where an island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: One connected land mass top-left, one isolated bottom-right.

fields.title: Flood Fill
fields.description: Given an image represented by an m x n grid of integers, a starting pixel, and a new color, perform a flood fill starting from that pixel, replacing connected pixels of the same original color.

examples.explanation: Connected region of 1s starting at (1,1) recolored to 2.
Target color already matches, no change needed.

fields.title: Clone Graph
fields.description: Given a reference of a node in a connected undirected graph, return a deep copy (clone) of the graph, preserving all node values and edges.
constraints: The graph has no repeated edges or self-loops.

examples.explanation: A deep copy with identical structure is produced.
Single node with no neighbors is cloned as-is.

fields.title: Course Schedule
fields.description: There are numCourses courses labeled 0 to numCourses-1. Given prerequisite pairs, determine if it is possible to finish all courses (i.e., the prerequisite graph has no cycle).

fields.title: Graph Valid Tree
fields.description: Given n nodes labeled 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges, determine if these edges form a valid tree (connected and acyclic).

examples.explanation: Connected with exactly n-1 edges and no cycle.

fields.title: Climbing Stairs
fields.description: You are climbing a staircase with n steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. Return the number of distinct ways to reach the top.

fields.title: House Robber
fields.description: Given an array representing money in houses along a street, determine the maximum amount you can rob without robbing two adjacent houses.

fields.title: Coin Change
fields.description: Given an array of coin denominations and a target amount, return the fewest number of coins needed to make up that amount, or -1 if impossible.

fields.title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
fields.description: Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

fields.title: Unique Paths
fields.description: A robot is located at the top-left corner of an m x n grid and can only move down or right. Return the number of unique paths to reach the bottom-right corner.
constraints: Answer is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit integer.

examples.explanation: 3 distinct paths exist in a 3x2 grid.

fields.title: Binary Search
fields.description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers nums and a target value, return the index of target if found, or -1 otherwise, in O(log n) time.
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order.

fields.title: Find Minimum in Rotated Sorted Array
fields.description: Given a rotated sorted array of unique elements, find the minimum element in O(log n) time.

examples.explanation: The array was rotated at index 3, minimum is 1.
Minimum value is 0 at the rotation point.

fields.title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
fields.description: Given a rotated sorted array nums and a target value, return the index of target if it exists, else -1, in O(log n) time.
constraints: All values in nums are unique.

fields.title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
fields.description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array (the kth largest in sorted order, not the kth distinct element).

examples.explanation: 4th largest value in sorted order is 4.

fields.title: Merge Sorted Array
fields.description: Given two sorted integer arrays nums1 and nums2, merge nums2 into nums1 as one sorted array in-place, where nums1 has extra trailing space to accommodate the merge.

examples.explanation: nums2 merged in-place into nums1's sorted order.

fields.title: Subsets
fields.description: Given an integer array nums of unique elements, return all possible subsets (the power set). The solution set must not contain duplicate subsets.

fields.title: Generate Parentheses
fields.description: Given n pairs of parentheses, generate all combinations of well-formed parentheses.

examples.explanation: Only one valid combination for a single pair.

fields.title: Permutations
fields.description: Given an array nums of distinct integers, return all possible permutations in any order.

fields.title: Combination Sum
fields.description: Given an array of distinct integers candidates and a target integer, return all unique combinations where the chosen numbers sum to target. The same number may be reused unlimited times.

examples.explanation: Both combinations sum to 7 using reusable candidates.
No combination of 2s can sum to 1.

fields.title: N-Queens
fields.description: The n-queens puzzle is the problem of placing n queens on an n x n chessboard such that no two queens attack each other. Return all distinct solutions.

examples.explanation: Two distinct valid placements exist for a 4x4 board.
Trivially one placement for a 1x1 board.

fields.title: Contains Duplicate
fields.description: Given an integer array nums, return true if any value appears at least twice in the array, and false if every element is distinct.

fields.title: Ransom Note
fields.description: Given two strings ransomNote and magazine, return true if ransomNote can be constructed by using the letters from magazine, each letter used at most once.
constraints: Both consist of lowercase English letters.

examples.explanation: magazine has enough letters to build ransomNote.

fields.title: Isomorphic Strings
fields.description: Given two strings s and t, determine if they are isomorphic, meaning characters in s can be replaced to get t while preserving a consistent one-to-one mapping.

examples.explanation: e->a and g->d form a consistent bijective mapping.
'o' would need to map to both 'a' and 'r'.

fields.title: Top K Frequent Elements
fields.description: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the k most frequent elements. The answer may be returned in any order.
constraints: k is in range [1, number of distinct elements]

examples.explanation: 1 appears 3 times, 2 appears twice — the top 2 most frequent.

fields.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
fields.description: Given an unsorted array of integers nums, return the length of the longest consecutive elements sequence, achievable in O(n) time.
